topics.text: Location-Based Effects are special effects that activate and deactivate depending on where the owner of the Enchanted Item moves. Location-Based Effects trigger only when such items are initially equipped and subsequently when the owning Entity moves to a new space in the Block grid - i.e. when their coordinates change to a new integer value.

topics.text: Most Enchantment effects are filtered using Conditions (same types as in loot tables). This enables effects to be specific for different situations. Each Effect Component defines which parameters are available for the condition to evaluate - some parameters are available for all of these parameter sets, while some are specific to a certain set. Each effect component specifies which parameters are available in the Effect Components list below.

topics.text: Text Components are no longer stored as JSON wrapped by a string.
topics.reason: release-note behaviour presented or consumed by the client

topics.text: The format itself is the same as before, but inlined directly into the outer structure.
topics.reason: release-note behaviour presented or consumed by the client

topics.text: For example, the item component minecraft:custom_name="{"text":"Renamed item"}" will become minecraft:custom_name={text:'Renamed item'}.
topics.reason: release-note behaviour presented or consumed by the client

topics.text: This includes Text Components passed as arguments to commands such as /tellraw or /title.
topics.reason: release-note behaviour presented or consumed by the client

topics.text: Note: in the case where Text Components are embedded in NBT, no distinction exists between boolean and integer types.
topics.reason: release-note behaviour presented or consumed by the client

topics.text: For Text Components with the NBT type and interpret set to true, Text Components will be parsed from the given NBT directly rather than converting to string and parsing as JSON.

topics.text: Time markers will exist within the context of a specific world clock. This means that even though the different time markers are defined by different Timelines, only one Time Marker can exist with a particular id for a particular world clock.
